title: Pradeep Rawat, Bollywood's Iconic Villain From Lagaan and Ghajini, Dies at 74
excerpt: The veteran character actor, known for menacing roles across Hindi, Telugu and Tamil cinema, had been battling blood cancer.
body:
• Veteran actor Pradeep Rawat died on August 4, 2026, in Mumbai after battling blood cancer. He was 74.
  • Best known for his menacing roles in Lagaan (2001) and both the Tamil and Hindi versions of Ghajini, Rawat worked across five Indian film industries over four decades.
  • His career spanned more than 100 films, beginning with a breakthrough role as Ashwatthama in B.R. Chopra's landmark television series Mahabharat.
  • Co-star Yashpal Sharma confirmed the news on social media, calling Rawat a friend, colleague, and irreplaceable presence in Indian cinema.

Pradeep Rawat, the character actor whose hulking frame and gravelly voice made him one of Indian cinema's most recognisable villains, died in Mumbai on Tuesday. He was 74 and had been receiving treatment for blood cancer, according to industry colleagues, though his family has not released a formal statement on the cause of death.

A Career Built on Menace

Born in Jabalpur on January 21, 1952, Rawat first came to national attention playing Ashwatthama in B.R. Chopra's Mahabharat, the television epic that held India captive in the late 1980s. He carried that mythological intensity into a film career that would stretch across Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam cinema.

His turn as the corrupt cop in John Matthew Matthan's Sarfarosh (1999) opposite Aamir Khan announced him as a heavyweight screen villain. Two years later, he played Deva, the menacing thug in Ashutosh Gowariker's Oscar-nominated Lagaan — a role that brought him before a global audience for the first time.

"He was more than a colleague. He was a friend who lived and breathed cinema. The screen will feel emptier without him."

— Yashpal Sharma, actor and Lagaan co-star

The Ghajini Breakthrough

Rawat's defining role came in A.R. Murugadoss's Tamil thriller Ghajini (2005), where he played both the protagonist and the terrifying antagonist Ghajini Dharmatma in a dual role that showcased his range. The film became a massive hit, and when it was remade in Hindi in 2008 with Aamir Khan in the lead, Rawat reprised his villain role, cementing his place in Bollywood's gallery of memorable antagonists.

S.S. Rajamouli's sports drama Sye (2004) earned him the Filmfare Best Villain Award in Telugu, along with the Nandi Award — rare recognition for an actor who spent most of his career in the shadows of leading men.

Four Decades Across Five Industries

What set Rawat apart was his versatility across languages. He moved between Telugu blockbusters like Nenu Sailaja and Sarrainodu and Hindi comedies like Grand Masti with equal ease. He debuted in Kannada with Parodi, in Malayalam with China Town, and even took on Bengali and Bhojpuri cinema. By the time he stepped back from active work, his filmography ran to well over 100 titles.

In recent years, Rawat had appeared in Telugu releases including Jatadhara and maintained a presence in the industry through events and interviews. His candid personality occasionally made headlines — a 2025 interview where he discussed a rumoured rift with Salman Khan drew widespread attention.

Tributes Pour In

Actor Yashpal Sharma, who shared the screen with Rawat in Lagaan, was among the first to publicly mourn his passing, posting a tribute on Instagram that recalled their decades-long friendship. Industry figures across South and North Indian cinema have begun sharing condolences, celebrating a performer who elevated every villain he played into something audiences could not look away from.

Rawat is survived by his wife Kalyani and their two children.
